title: Antigen presentation by CD40+MHC-II+ astrocytes promotes CNS autoimmunity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded 7 of 10 Zenodo files (CC-BY-4.0, no login) and listed the 3 large ones by a ranged read of their zip directories. Opened and counted: the cell-contact matrix EAE.T.Cells.Astrocytes.network.csv (902 T cells x 1,652 astrocytes, all values 0/1, 38,510 contact edges, 829/902 T cells and 1,290/1,652 astrocytes with at least one edge), its metadata (2,554 cells, 18 columns, 4 mice, 15 samples, 2 pools, no gene columns), the larger network (1,643 x 18,353; 21,871-cell metadata with only a cell-type column), four gene-level differential-expression tables (21,169 / 13,083 / 1,611,971-byte files with genes, log2 fold change, p, adjusted p), the proximity-proteomics summary (1,388 proteins, UniProt IDs, log2 fold change; only 17 with adjusted p < 0.05), the full mass-spectrometry workbooks (2,220 protein groups, 6 CD40-BioID2 vs 3 control LFQ intensity columns, 56 proteins passing SAINTexpress), and the AlphaFold-Multimer score sheet (1,120 prediction rows over ~224 protein pairs, 79 'positive' rows). Queried NCBI GEO/SRA/BioProject links for PubMed 42557325 and PRIDE for a proteomics deposit: none exist.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental design (rabies-barcode contact mapping, SorTag-based contact labelling, in vivo CRISPR knockouts, multiple sclerosis single-nucleus data) comes from the abstract plus the data-availability statement on the publisher page; the full text is paywalled and not in PubMed Central, so no methods, figure counts or sample tables were read. The data-availability statement itself states that only 'analysis results and bioinformatics data' are on Zenodo and 'all other data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request'.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record 19803100 is open, CC-BY-4.0, and downloaded on the first try; but it holds only derived results. The paper's own single-cell, single-nucleus, bulk RNA and mass-spectrometry data have no GEO, SRA or PRIDE accession (checked) and are 'on reasonable request'.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The contact label is a real matrix: 902 x 1,652 zeros and ones, so 'did this T cell touch this astrocyte' is one row-sum away. Verified in EAE.T.Cells.Astrocytes.network.csv.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. No gene-expression values for any of the 2,554 barcoded cells are deposited; the metadata file has 18 columns, all quality-control or cluster fields (counts, features, percent mitochondrial, cluster number), and zero genes. The only expression content is pre-computed differential-expression summaries, which cannot serve as per-cell features.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated where they exist: LFQ (label-free quantification) intensity columns, log2 fold change, TPM (transcripts per million), SAINTscore and BFDR (Bayesian false-discovery rate). Checked in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL for every task whose inputs are actually present. Proximity proteomics: 2,220 protein groups but only 56 positives after SAINTexpress and 17 proteins with adjusted p < 0.05 in the 1,388-row table. Knockout experiments: 4 differential-expression comparisons (the unit is the perturbation, not the gene). Sorted-astrocyte bulk RNA: 8 samples. AlphaFold pairs: ~224. The 1.49M labelled cell pairs are the only large set, and they have no features.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything tabular is under 60 MB; working set well under 1 GB. Only the 500 MB Seurat R object (c_TDTOMATO) is large, and I recorded it by name and size rather than downloading it.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No contradictions found, but nothing could be cross-checked either: the full text is paywalled, so the 1,652 astrocytes / 902 T cells and 2,220 protein groups I counted have no published figure to be compared against.

a8_label_provenance.note: The contact label is a physical measurement (shared rabies barcodes read out by sequencing) and the proteomics label is mass-spectrometry intensity, so neither is a model output. One caveat: the AlphaFold-Multimer score sheet (pIS, LIS, ipTM) is entirely another model's output and would fail A8 if used as a target.

existing_models.name: Gloss (Group Lasso on scRNA-seq), Azad et al., Cell Reports Methods 2026 - links a cell's transcriptome to how strongly it physically interacted with a partner cell
existing_models.score_and_split: Reports R-squared on held-out cells over 50 random 80/20 train-test splits with 5-fold nested cross-validation for tuning; beats correlation, ridge, lasso and elastic-net baselines (numbers read from the article page, not re-run).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Their framing is that interaction-strength readouts are still scarce and that moving from gene associations to causal mediators of contact remains open.

existing_models.name: GEARS, Roohani et al., Nature Biotechnology 2023 - predicts the transcriptome-wide response to knocking out a gene
existing_models.score_and_split: Published on Perturb-seq screens with unseen-perturbation splits; a 2025 Nature Methods re-evaluation (Ahlmann-Eltze et al.) found it and single-cell foundation models do not beat predicting the mean across training perturbations.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalising to perturbations of genes never seen in training.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell transcriptome models) would be the natural backbone for the contact-prediction task; ESM-2 (protein language model) for the proteomics task
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would suffice for the small tables, but there is nothing to embed: no per-cell expression matrix is deposited, and the protein task has 56 positives.
backbone.licence: Zenodo deposit is CC-BY-4.0, so reuse of the derived tables is unrestricted.

integration.partner_dataset: GSE150858 (the 2021 RABID-seq rabies-barcode contact dataset from the same lab, public) plus GSE275471 and GSE253000 (the public contact-intensity datasets used by the Gloss model)
integration.join_key: mouse gene symbol / Ensembl gene ID for genes; UniProt accession for the proteomics table
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a model trained on one lab's barcode-based cell-contact data predict which cells touched each other in a different contact assay - but this paper contributes only summary statistics to that question, because its own per-cell expression is not released.

controls.positive_control: Would have been easy if features existed: the model must recover Cd40, H2-Ab1 and T helper 17 genes as markers of contact-experienced cells, since the paper reports them. With only summary tables, there is nothing to run the control on.
controls.negative_control: Shuffling the 0/1 contact matrix is possible, but pointless without features to pair it with.
controls.external_validation: GSE150858 (the lab's earlier barcode-contact dataset) is public and would be the external set; none of this paper's own data can be validated against it.

honest_claim_h3: Nothing can honestly be claimed from a model built on this deposit: the only large label set (38,510 measured cell-cell contacts among 1.49M possible pairs) comes with no measurements of the cells themselves, so any model would be predicting contact from quality-control statistics such as read count.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a cell's gene-activity profile to predict whether it physically touched an astrocyte during brain autoimmune disease.
plain_idea.train_on: Intended input: the gene-activity profile of each immune cell and each astrocyte recovered from inflamed mouse spinal cord. The contact labels exist for 902 T cells x 1,652 astrocytes (1.49M pairs, 38,510 measured contacts), but the gene profiles for those exact cells are not in the deposit.
plain_idea.predict: Output: a probability that a given T cell and astrocyte were in physical contact. The true answer comes from a barcoded rabies virus that spreads from astrocytes to touching cells, so two cells carrying the same barcode are recorded as having touched.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups studying multiple sclerosis would get a way to flag contact-experienced cells in ordinary single-cell datasets, where no barcode is available; even a failure would quantify how much of physical contact is visible in a transcriptome at all.

more_or_better_data.why: Gloss was developed on public contact-intensity datasets (GSE275471, GSE253000) with full expression matrices; this paper offers 38,510 contact edges with no expression at all, so it is strictly less usable, not more.

confidence_score.why: There are 4 mice and 2 sequencing pools in the contact metadata, which could in principle support per-group uncertainty, but with no features there is no prediction to attach a confidence to.

models_beatable.why: Gloss is a 2026 method with open code and repeated held-out-cell evaluation; GEARS-style perturbation models were re-benchmarked honestly in Nature Methods in 2025. Both are current and evaluated on splits we could not improve on with these files.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The first condition already fails: we cannot give our model everything the baseline sees, because the per-cell expression matrix the baseline requires is not deposited.

ml_idea: Intended project: predict from a single cell's transcriptome whether it physically contacted an astrocyte, training on rabies-barcode contact labels, with a scGPT or Geneformer backbone frozen and a small classifier head, held out by mouse. The project cannot be built from this paper because the contact labels are released without the matching expression matrices; a fallback task (predicting CD40 proximity-interactome membership from ESM-2 protein embeddings) has only 56 positive proteins out of 2,220 quantified.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed beyond the loads I ran: the contact matrix (902 x 1,652) and all differential-expression tables load in seconds and together occupy well under 1 GB; the only heavy object, a 500 MB Seurat R file, was deliberately not downloaded.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Print the column names of EAE.T.Cells.Astrocytes.network.meta.tsv: 18 columns, all quality-control or cluster fields, zero genes. That single command kills the project in under a minute.

verdict_reason: A3 fails: the measured cell-cell contact labels (38,510 edges over 902 T cells x 1,652 astrocytes) are deposited without any per-cell gene expression, and the paper's sequencing and proteomics data have no GEO, SRA or PRIDE accession - they are 'available from the corresponding author on reasonable request'. A5 also fails for every task whose inputs do exist: 56 positive proteins out of 2,220 in the CD40 proximity proteomics, 4 knockout comparisons, 8 sorted-astrocyte bulk samples, ~224 AlphaFold-Multimer pairs (whose scores are a model's output anyway, so they would fail A8 as labels). The Zenodo record is genuinely open and tidy, but it is a set of figure-backing summaries, not a modelling dataset.
